text:
Nick Suzuki is coming off the best season of his career, 101 points and the Selke Trophy, and Evolving-Hockey ranked him fourth among all forwards in value. This year's start is solid rather than spectacular: 9 goals and 20 points in 20 games, eight on the power play, more than 20 minutes a night against top lines.

The recent stretch is the concern. He has five points in his last ten games against roughly 10.5 we'd expect at his ice time, with his on-ice chances running below his usual rate and his ice time down almost two minutes. His own shooting, 17.6%, is actually above our talent range, so the goals aren't the issue; the setup work is.

The power play is part of it. Sportsnet's Eric Engels noted Suzuki said "it's definitely not broken" on Nov. 17, then watched it struggle that night. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 89th percentile in shot assists last season. Shot assists are the earliest sign of assists to come, and the number to watch.
headline: Suzuki's quiet stretch runs through the setup work
